markup: If the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is 90⁰, what are the values of the angle of incidence and angle of reflection?
answermarkup:
Given : Angle between the incident ray and reflected ray is 100⁰
                     ⟹   ∠i + ∠r = 90⁰
To find : Angle of reflection (∠r) and angle of incidence (∠i)
Formula : ∠i = ∠r
                  Given that, ∠i + ∠r = 90⁰
          ∴  ∠i + ∠i = 90⁰       ⟹  2 ∠i = 90⁰
           ∴ ∠i  = 90/2 = 45⁰
           The angle of incidence is 45⁰ and angle of reflection is 45⁰.

Derive the formula for coefficient of linear expansion.
answermarkup:
When a rod of length l₁ is heated from temperature T₁ to temperature T₂ this shows the expansion of length.
If the length after expansion is l₂ then, change in length α (original length) × (Change in temperature) 
∴ l₂ - l₁ α l₁ × ΔT
∴ l₂ - l₁ = λ (l₁ × ΔT)      ⟹  l₂ = l₁ (1 + λΔT) --------- (i)
Here, λ = constant of proportionality, coefficient of linear expansion. This coefficient of linear expansion is different for different materials. From (i) we get, 
λ = (l₂ - l₁)/l₁ΔT

Explain osmosis with examples.
answermarkup:
Osmosis is the physical process by which water travels from a part or region having higher water concentration to a part with lesser water concentration through a selectively permeable membrane. With reference to a cell, osmosis can occur in the following ways : 
i) Isotonic solution: When the medium outside and inside the cell has the same water concentration, there is no movement of water molecules in either direction. 
ii) Hypotonic solution (Endosmosis): When the cell has a lesser water concentration than the outside medium, water enters the cell by endosmosis. e.g. Raisins kept in water swell and become turgid after sometime. 
iii) Hypertonic solution (Exosmosis): When the cell has a higher water concentration than the outside medium, water moves out of the cell by exosmosis. e.g. Contraction of cytoplasm and loss of water from an animal cell kept in a hypertonic solution.

markup: Explain the life cycle of a star having mass twice as that of the Sun.

i) Stars having initial mass less than 8 times mass of the Sun evolve to undergo huge expansion. 
ii) Their radius increases by a factor of 100 to 200. They become large in size and look reddish due to their lower temperature. Hence, they are called red giant stars. 
iii) At the end of its evolution, red giant stars explode and their outer gas envelope is thrown out. Inner part of stars contract reducing it to a size similar to that of the earth. 
iv) As mass of the star is much higher than that of the earth while its size is similar to that of the earth, density of the star becomes very high. 
v) At this stage, pressure due to electrons in the star becomes independent of temperature and balances its gravitational force. 
vi) In this stage, star looks white and due to its small size, it is called as white dwarf. 
vii) After this its temperature keeps decreasing but its size and mass no longer change. Hence, white dwarf is the end stage of stars having initial mass less than 8 times mass of the Sun.

markup: Study the figure given below and describe it briefly :
answermarkup:
i) The given picture represents the interactions among the different factors of an ecosystem.
ii) Ecosystem consists of biotic and abiotic factors. Both these factors continuously interact with each other. The biotic and abiotic factors and the interactions between them form an ecosystem.
iii) Biotic (living) factors include producers, consumers and decomposers, whereas abiotic (non-living) factors include chemical factors like organic and inorganic substances and physical factors like sunlight, water, etc.
iv) In an ecosystem, the abiotic factors determine the survival of biotic factors.
v) Producers (plants) are autotrophic, they depend on abiotic factors like sunlight, water, soil, minerals, etc. for photosynthesis. Energy produced during this process enters the ecosystem through the producers.
vi) Primary consumers (herbivores) depend on producers for their food and the secondary consumers depend on the primary consumers. The tertiary consumers depend on secondary consumers. The primary consumers play a major role in transfer of energy from plants to other biotic factors in an ecosystem.
vii) Decomposers breakdown the dead remains of plants and animals and make nutrients available in the ecosystem.
viii) The sequence of transfer of energy from producers to decomposers forms a food chain and removal any of these factors can disrupt the entire food chain.
ix) Thus, biotic and abiotic factors interact and work together in an ecosystem. They play a major role in the maintenance of the ecosystem.

markup: Write a short note on specific heat of a substance.
answermarkup:
Specific heat:
i) The specific heat of a substance is the amount of heat required to increase the temperature of unit mass of the substance through one degree.
ii) It is denoted by letter c.
iii) The S.I. unit of specific heat is J/kg⁰C and C.G.S. unit is cal/g⁰C.
iv) The amount of heat (Q) required to raise the temperature of object of mass m and specific heat c from initial temperature Ti to temperature Tf is given by, Q = m × c × (Tf - Ti)
v) Examples: Specific heat of water is 1cal /g⁰C while that of gold is 0.03cal /g⁰C

markup: A bridge is made from 20 m long iron rods. At temperature 18⁰C, the distance between two rods is 0.4 cm. Up to what temperature will the bridge be in good shape?
answermarkup:
Length of the rod = 20 m (l₁)
Length of the rod after expansion = 20.004 m(l₂)
Initial temperature = 18⁰C (T₁) , Final temperature = T₂ 
T₂ - T₁ = ΔT
Coefficient of Linear expansion of Iron = 11.5 × 10⁻⁶ l/⁰C
l₂ = l₁ (1 + λΔT)
20.004 = 20[1 + (11.5 × 10⁻⁶)ΔT]
1 + 11.5 × 10⁻⁶ ΔT = 20.004/20
1 +11.5 × 10⁻⁶ ΔT = 1.0002
ΔT = 0.0002/(11.5 × 10⁻⁶)
      = T₂ - T₁ = 17.4
      = T₂ - 18 = 17.4 
ΔT = T₂ = 17.4 + 18 = 35.4 
The bridge will be in good shape upto the temperature 35.4⁰C.

iii)  It means that they are set into periodic motion in forward and backward direction.
iv) If during the vibration, the prongs of the tuning fork go away from each other, the air outside the prongs is compressed and the pressure there increases.
v) Such a state of high pressure is created in region A.
vi)  The region in which air is at high pressure and high density is called compression.
vii) In the next step of vibration, the prongs of the fork come close to (a) each other.
viii)  In this case, the air molecules near the prongs get more space to move
away from each other. 
ix) As a result, the air pressure in this region (Region A) decreases.
x)  Such region in which air is at low pressure and low density is called rarefaction. 
xi) Such a periodic motion of creates compression prongs and rarefaction and these are propagated away from the prongs. These are the sound waves.
xii) When these waves reach our ear, the ear - drum vibrates; accordingly, specific signals reach our brain and sound is heard.

answermarkup:
a) Regular reflection of light: 
i) The reflection of light from a plane and smooth surface is called regular reflection of light. 
ii) The angles of incidence and the angles of reflection are same for all parallel rays falling on the surface. 
iii) Hence, the reflected rays are also parallel to incident rays. 
iv) If i₁, i₂, i₃ … in represent the angles of incidence and r₁, r₂, r₃ ……. rₙ represent the angles of reflection, then i₁ = r₁, i₂ = r₂, …… iₙ = rₙ and i₁ = i₂ = i₃ …… = iₙ = r₁ = r₂ = r₃ ……. rₙ
b) Irregular reflection of light: 
i) Reflection of light from a rough surface is called irregular reflection of light. 
ii) The angles of incidence for all parallel incident rays are not equal in irregular reflection. 
iii) Hence, the angles of reflection are also not equal. Thus, the reflected rays do not travel parallel to one another but they spread over a larger area. 
iv) If i₁, i₂, i₃ …… iₙ represent the angles of incidence and r₁, r₂, r₃…… rₙ represent the angles of reflection, then iᵢ = rᵢ, i₂ = r₂ … iₙ = rₙ but iᵢ  i₂  i₃… iₙ and r₁  r₂  r₃… rₙ

markup: Write a short note on Nuclear Reactor.
answermarkup:
a) A nuclear reactor is a machine that generates electricity on a large scale by using atomic energy. 
b) Working of nuclear reactor: i) In a nuclear reactor, the nucleus of the isotope uranium-235, on bombardment with slow speed of neutrons, undergoes nuclear fission to form nuclei of two different elements, krypton-92 and barium-141 and 2 to 3 neutrons. 
ii) On decreasing the speed and number, these neutrons bring about fission of more uranium-235 nuclei and thus, a chain reaction of nuclear fission takes place. 
iii) A large amount of nuclear energy in the form of heat isreleased during a chain reaction of fission. 
iv) The chain reaction is kept under control to prevent any probable explosion. c) To control the chain reaction in the nuclear reactor, it is necessary to decrease the speed and number of neutrons, used for the bombardment on U-235 isotope. The following provisions are made in a nuclear reactor in order to avoid explosion: 
1) Moderator: Graphite or heavy water is used as moderator for reducing the speed of neutrons. 
2) Controller: Rods of boron, cadmium, beryllium, etc. are used as controller for reducing the number of neutrons by absorbing them. 
3) Coolant: The nuclear fission process produces large amount of heat which is taken out by using water as coolant.

markup: Explain Expansion of solids.
answermarkup:
i) When heat is given to any substance, its temperature increases and it expands. Its expansion depends on the increase in its temperature.
ii) Expansion of solids:
a) Linear Expansion: The linear expansion of a solid is the increase in length of a wire or a rod of a solid due to increase in its temperature. When we increase the temperature of a rod of length l₁ from T₁ to T₂ its length becomes l₂ The change in length is proportional to the original length and the increase in temperature (ΔT = T₂ - T₁)
∴ Change in the length α original length x Change in temperature 
∴ l₂ - l₁ α l₁ × ΔT
∴ l₂ - l₁ = λ × l₁ × ΔT
∴ l₂ = l₁ (1 + λΔT)
Here, λ is the constant of proportionality and it is called the coefficient of linear expansion of the solid substance.
b) Areal Expansion of solids: The area of a sheet of a solid material also increases on heating. This is called areal expansion of solids. This is given by the formula: 
A₂ = A₁(l + σΔT)
 Here, ΔT is the change in the temperature and A₁ and A₂ are the initial and the final areas of the sheet, σ is the coefficient of areal expansion of the solid.
c) Volumetric expansion of solids: A three dimensional piece of solid expands on all sides when heated and its volume increases this is called the volumetric expansion of solids. This is given by the formula: V₂ = V₁(1 + βΔT) 
Here, ΔT is the change in the temperature and V₁ and V₂ are the initial and final volumes of the solid. ẞ is the volumetric expansion coefficient of the solid.

markup: Explain the functional correlation of circulatory system with respiratory digestive and excretory system.
answermarkup:

ii) The inhaled oxygen during respiration reaches alveoli and is diffused into the blood. This diffused oxygen is then transported to the cells in various parts of the body for cellular respiration.
iii) Carbon dioxide being a waste product of cellular respiration is diffused in the alveoli, which is transported into the bronchioles and reaches trachea through bronchi. From there it is exhaled out of the body through nose.
iv) The circulatory system needs the organs of the digestive system to transport nutrients to the body cells. Simple nutrients like glucose, fatty acids, amino acids, etc., are carried by the blood from the wall of alimentary canal to each cell of the body.
v) Ammonia, urea, creatinine, etc. are nitrogenous wastes, which are released by the tissues for excretion, carried by blood.
vi) In this way, different body systems like circulatory, respiratory, digestive and excretory systems are functionally correlated.

markup: Write the postulates of Bohr’s atomic model.
answermarkup:
In the year 1913, Danish scientist : Niels Bohr explained the stability of atom by putting stable orbit atomic model. The important postulates of Bohr’s atomic model are as follows :
i) The electrons revolving around the atomic nucleus lie in the concentric circular orbits at certain distance from the nucleus.
ii) Energy of an electron is constant while it is in a particular orbit.
iii) When an electron jumps from an inner orbit to an outer orbit, it absorbs energy equal to the difference of its energy level and when it jumps from outer orbit to an inner orbit, it emits energy equal to the difference of its energy level.
iv) The stationary orbits are numbered as 1, 2, 3, 4, …. or by letters K, L, M, N respectively.
v) The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in nth orbit is 2n².

markup: What is an ecosystem? Explain the effects of increased population on the ecosystem in detail.
answermarkup:

                   OR 
The structure formed due to reciprocal relationships between living organisms, their habitat and environment is called as ecosystem. 
b) Following are the effects of increased population on ecosystems: 
1) Depletion of natural resources: Increase in population has led to an increase in the demand for natural resources. Ecosystems can fulfil basic requirements of humans but large scale increase in population and change in lifestyle of humans has lead to over- exploitation of natural resources. This has created stress on the ecosystems and has generated large amount of wastes. Burden of waste disposal has also created stress on ecosystems. 
2) Threat to biodiversity / Loss of biodiversity: Due to rapid urbanization, industrialization, etc., more and more forest areas are being cleared. Destruction of agricultural lands, marshlands, wetlands, forests and grasslands for construction of buildings, roads, dams, etc., have either changed or destroyed ecosystems. markup: Explain Rutherford’s atomic model.

iii) Negatively charged particles called electrons revolve around the nucleus.

markup: Explain different types of inertia.
answermarkup:
Different types of inertia are inertia of the state of rest, inertia of motion and directional inertia.
i) Inertia of the state of rest : An object in the state of rest cannot change in its state of rest due to its inherent property. This property is called inertia of state of rest. For e.g. Fruits fall down due to inertia of rest when the branches of a tree are shaken.
ii) Inertia of motion : The inherent property of an object due to which its state of motion cannot change is called inertia of motion. For e.g. passengers sitting in the running bus get a jerk in the forward direction if the bus suddenly stops
iii) Directional inertia : The inherent property of an object due to which the object cannot change the direction of its motion, is called directional inertia. For e.g. if a vehicle in motion along a straight line suddenly turns, the passenger sitting in it are thrown opposite to the direction of turning.

markup: Explain the end stages of star.
answermarkup:
Stars can be classified based on their mass and end stages : 
1) Stars having initial mass less than 8 times the mass of the sun (M star
< 8 M sun): Stars in this group undergo huge expansion and their radius increases by a factor of 100 to 200. This is called as red giant stars. At the end of the evolution, these stars explode and their outer gas envelope is thrown out. In this stage, star looks white and due to its small size it is called white dwarf. 
2) Stars having initial mass between 8 and 25 time the mass of the sun: These stars also go through red giant stage and later through supergiant stage during which their size may increase 1000 times. Huge explosion called supernova explosion is very powerful. Finally, the central portion of star which is left behind is made of neutrons and is called neutron stars.
Neutron star is the end stage of this star.
3) Stars having mass larger than 25 times the mass of sun: These stars evolve like the stars in the second group but after the supernova explosion, no pressure is capable of balancing their huge gravitational force and they continue contracting for ever. Their gravitational force increases tremendously. Thus, we cannot see the star at all but can probably see a minute black hole. The end stage of this star is therefore called a black hole.

markup: Answer the following questions : a) Define Buoyant force. A plastic cube is released in water will it sink or come to the surface of water.          b) If density of water is 10³ kg/m³ and density of copper is 7.5 × 10³ kg/m³. calculate relative density of copper.

iv) Density of plastic is less than that of water. Hence, the buoyant force exerted by water on the plastic cube will be more than the weight of the plastic cube causing the plastic cube to come to the surface. Hence, a plastic cube released in water will come to the surface of water.

Formula: Relative density = Density of copper/ Density of water 
Calculation: From formula, Relative density = (7.52 ×10³)/ 10³  = 7.52 
Ans: The relative density of copper is 7.52

markup: Describe the construction and working of an electric bell with the help of a diagram.

Construction 
i) An Electric bell consists of an insulated copper wire, which is coiled around the horse shoe shaped iron core.
ii) One end of the coil of wire is connected to one end of an electric cell. 
iii) When electric current flows through the coil, it behaves like a magnet.
iv) A flexible iron strip is placed in front of this magnet.
v) A metal striker is attached to this strip. This striker can strike a metal gong.
vi) The other pole of the cell is connected to a contact screw through a switch. vii) The flexible metal strip is in contact with the screw.
Working
i) When we press the switch, circuit is completed. When screw is in contact with the strip electric current flows through the coil making the core and electromagnet.
ii) At once, it attracts the flexible iron strip and the striker hits the gong and sound is produced.
iii) However, in this position the contact of the strip with the screw breaks and current stops.
iv) At this time, the coil loses its magnetism and flexible strip moves back and makes contact with the screw.
v) This causes the current to flow again and again and striker hits the gong.
vi) This make and break of current keeps the bell ringing till the switch is pressed.

markup: Describe numerical method for the formation of ionic bond is sodium chloride.
answermarkup:
i) Sodium chloride is formed from its constituent elements, sodium ( 11 Na ) and chlorine ( 17 Cl )
ii) The electronic configuration of sodium is (2, 8, 1) and that of chlorine is (2, 8, 7).
iii) The valency of sodium is 1 as it has one electron in valence shell (M-shell). The valency of chlorine is 1 as it has 7 electrons in its valence shell (M-shell) and it just needs one electron to complete the octet.
iv) Sodium loses its valence electron from M-shell and hence, the penultimate L-shell becomes the outermost shell which has 8 electrons in it. Thus, sodium attains a complete electron octet.
v) On loss of one electron, the number of electrons in sodium becomes 10. Therefore, the total positive charge of +11 on sodium nucleus is imbalanced. Thus, a Na⁺ cation which carries net positive charge +1 is formed.
vi) Similarly, chlorine gains one electron to complete its octet in M-shell. However, the charge is imbalanced on chlorine nucleus. Thus, a CI⁻ anion which carries net negative charge -1 is formed.
vii) When elements of sodium and chlorine combine, a sodium atom gives its valence electron to a chlorine atom. In the process, cation and CI⁻ anion are formed. Na⁺
viii) These oppositely charged cations and anions are attracted by electrostatic force of attraction resulting in the formation of a chemical bond which is also called ionic bond or electrovalent bond.

Different human activities have different effects on ecosystems. There can be transformation of an ecosystem from one to another or extinction of a species. 
a) State any two human activities which affects ecosystem.           b) How does industrialization affect the ecosystem?             c) Name some natural diseases that affect ecosystem.
answermarkup:
a) Mining and deforestation are the two activities which affect the ecosystem.
b) Raw materials required for industrialization are obtained by destroying forests. This results in destruction of forests thereby affecting the ecosystem.
c) Floods, volcanoes, earthquakes and droughts.
